# Restore current, explicitly reusable South African municipal boundary evidence

Follow-up from [#436](https://github.com/ChengshuLi/WorldAtlas/issues/436). Review the exact 196 municipality IDs pinned below. Find and inspect a dated official Municipal Demarcation Board boundary release later than the documented 2018 demarcations, establish its territorial meaning, boundary vintage, full municipality roster, detached-territory coverage, and explicit reuse terms, then retain the lawful source or exact restoration instructions and hashes.

Acceptance:
- Match every exact subject ID to an official code/name and current legal boundary; report source vintage, license, parent and neighboring tier semantics.
- Check all multipart/component differences, including Saldanha Bay, Swartland and Overstrand, and resolve the Sol Plaatjie area discrepancy with boundary evidence rather than thresholds.
- Record per-unit confidence and unresolved gaps. If no suitable source can be reused, document the source/license blocker and a clear authority handoff.
- Preserve existing IDs and release pins. Do not change core geography or production data; submit a separate engineering proposal for any sourced correction.

Current 2020 geoBoundaries boundaries and the inspected MDB service dated 2016 are not accepted as present-day boundary proof. No history import or regional approval is authorized.

## Post-merge audit evidence — 2026-10-06 America/Los_Angeles

Auditor `01a10892-0782-7b13-902c-d8b4db6c155d`; original PR [#957](https://github.com/ChengshuLi/WorldAtlas/pull/957), immutable merge `fee84aba6940d04d98f3fe374645d8ec76dd0445`. This supplements the existing scope and preserves its IDs and machine contract.

Whole-file input mapping at baseline `93c901e1c0b44073233fd3d48d403985a0cf2c52` (unchanged at the merge): `atlas_part_28` → `data/geography/part-28.json`, 6,613,963 bytes, SHA-256 `2aab2f36aeeb651ee8e6cc656e9541ad14e2ced2ea8160e8700ad4dc950c379d`; `atlas_hierarchy` → `data/hierarchy.json`, 10,164,089 bytes, SHA-256 `568301690ef231a85856666b57876a5efe8d8c7c6e671a56d81307b2dc28b80b`. Evidence packet: `data/regional-review/regional-review-1f8d0c3f746b0f8e/` at the immutable merge. Its `sources/issue-436-scope.json` matches all 196 issue subjects; the 17 ZAF subjects in #435 are disjoint. All 48 parent IDs resolve in the pinned hierarchy.

Independent read-only checks: inspected all 28 changed files and exact bytes; reran the bounded source crosswalk twice, both byte-identical to retained SHA-256 `65e403b35d293a8d7a85d79a9699498b9f915eda65f152575f2bad35456ddb17`. All 196 pairs are valid; none is topologically identical to Atlas; eight have different component counts; maximum source-to-Atlas relative area difference is 0.01215004. Independently verified all 48 parent identities/child counts and seven metro geometry comparisons. Five metro pairs are topologically equal; Buffalo City and Ekurhuleni differ. Neither similarity nor difference establishes legal identity or authorizes deletion. The straight-edge WGS84 analytic rectangle control agrees within 1e-10 relative tolerance; invalid latitude and a wrong source hash are rejected.

Authenticated upstream GitHub contents at geoBoundaries commit `9469f09592ced973a3448cf66b6100b741b64c0d` confirm retained ADM2 geometry (SHA-256 `6cc504ad835b37823da687a3fd3f0cab63608a6c8a5ad906e1011f1554bbbbdd`, 32,530,325 bytes) and original metadata hashes. This is a 2020 reference, not current legal boundary approval. The original ADM3 is 50,705,428 bytes, above the 32 MiB review cap; the Auditor verified retained partitions but did not restore that original or independently establish their derivation from its full bytes.

Complete open/closed issue pagination and all three currently open PR file lists were checked. No active reservation or overlapping owned evidence prefix was found for this issue at the readiness check. #435 and #436 are closed with released reservations. Those closures and the prior accepted-with-limits source review are supporting history, not independent proof of current polygons or every proposed label.

Readiness: ready for the existing bounded source research, with at most two PRs and ownership only in `data/regional-review/south-africa-municipal-boundaries-436/`. Missing current licensed boundary evidence is the research objective, not permission to edit core geography. Reproduce the component findings from the retained crosswalk and compare with an independently restored, dated authoritative roster and polygons. The retained Stats SA table reports Sol Plaatjie/Sol Plaatje at 3,138.063 versus 3,311.600 km² (5.2403%); the Auditor did not re-fetch its primary PDF, so verify that comparison against the source before drawing a boundary conclusion. Success remains an exact 196-ID, licensed, dated evidence inventory with component/territory coverage and explicit unresolved limits or authority handoff; no production import or geography approval.
